title: Turnaround of a Dysfunctional Engineering Team
situation: Inherited an engineering team that had been without a manager for approximately six months. Relationships between development and business leadership had deteriorated, meetings were ineffective, and the team exhibited a strong us-versus-them mentality.
task: Restore team culture, improve stakeholder relationships, increase productivity, and establish effective engineering practices.
actions: Built trust through one-on-one conversations with team members and stakeholders.
Introduced structure and accountability into meetings and Scrum ceremonies.
Addressed behavioral and performance concerns.
Improved communication between engineering and business leadership.
Created a more collaborative and positive team environment.
results: Improved team morale and engagement.
Significantly improved stakeholder relationships.
Created productive and focused team meetings.
Increased overall team effectiveness and delivery performance.

title: Department-Wide GitHub Copilot Adoption
situation: AI-assisted development tools were available but adoption and effective usage varied greatly among team members.
task: Accelerate AI adoption and ensure teams were using GitHub Copilot effectively to improve productivity.
actions: Created training materials and best-practice guides.
Conducted training sessions for engineering, QA, and product teams.
Established recurring demonstrations of successful AI use cases.
Encouraged experimentation with coding agents and AI workflows.
Shared lessons learned across teams.
results: Rapid adoption of GitHub Copilot across teams.
Training materials were reused by other managers across the department.
Developer productivity increased approximately 30 percent.
Teams became significantly more comfortable leveraging AI tools.

title: Maintaining Delivery Through Major Downsizing
situation: The engineering organization experienced significant headcount reductions while delivery expectations remained largely unchanged.
task: Maintain delivery capacity and team effectiveness despite reduced staffing levels.
actions: Increased adoption of GitHub Copilot and AI-assisted workflows.
Leveraged coding agents for implementation tasks.
Encouraged automation of repetitive work.
Focused engineers on higher-value activities.
Improved planning and estimation with AI assistance.
results: Maintained overall delivery output.
Improved individual productivity by approximately 30 percent.
Successfully adapted engineering processes to reduced staffing levels.

title: Automating SOC 2 and ISO 27001 Evidence Collection
situation: SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audits required significant manual effort to collect and validate evidence across many systems.
task: Reduce audit preparation effort and improve evidence quality through automation.
actions: Developed agent-based evidence collection processes.
Leveraged MCP servers and Playwright automation.
Built automated evidence validation and gap analysis workflows.
Integrated AI-powered evaluation of collected evidence.
results: Automated approximately 80 percent of SOC 2 evidence collection.
Automated approximately 50 percent of ISO 27001 evidence collection.
Improved audit readiness and reduced manual effort.
Increased confidence in evidence quality and completeness.

title: Preparing 500 Engineers for AWS and Containerization
situation: Entrata was preparing for a major shift toward AWS and containerization technologies that were unfamiliar to many engineering teams.
task: Help approximately 500 developers successfully prepare for the transition.
actions: Organized company-wide training initiatives.
Coordinated learning paths and educational resources.
Worked across US and India engineering organizations.
Tracked completion and participation metrics.
results: More than 500 engineers participated.
Achieved approximately 98 percent completion.
Improved organizational readiness for cloud transformation.

title: Creating a Company-Wide Engineering Learning Program
situation: Engineering teams lacked a regular mechanism for sharing knowledge and learning from one another.
task: Create a sustainable process for cross-team learning and technical collaboration.
actions: Launched a weekly lunch-and-learn series.
Recruited engineers and architects as presenters.
Showcased new technologies and project demonstrations.
Facilitated knowledge sharing across teams.
results: Created a sustained culture of technical learning.
Improved visibility into projects across the organization.
Encouraged collaboration and innovation.

title: Rescuing a Failed Product Initiative
situation: A previous attempt at building a sample management and testing system had been unsuccessful.
task: Deliver a scalable replacement capable of handling complex testing workflows and large numbers of samples.
actions: Redesigned the system architecture.
Created a highly scalable sample management platform.
Implemented Excel-style formula support for laboratory testing workflows.
Focused heavily on usability and configurability.
results: Successfully managed tens of thousands of samples.
Simplified sample management workflows for users.
Received strong customer acceptance.

title: Illinois Department of Transportation Migration
situation: The Illinois Department of Transportation needed to migrate from a legacy system to a new materials and testing platform.
task: Implement the platform and migrate legacy operational data without disrupting business operations.
actions: Worked closely with customer stakeholders.
Planned and executed data migration activities.
Configured the platform to meet customer requirements.
Supported deployment and adoption efforts.
results: Successfully migrated legacy data.
Delivered the new platform successfully.
Improved operational capabilities for the customer.
